Task 3a execution record (143.001-T) -- UNCONDITIONAL, tests/ surface only.

SITE-ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION: this task's own description names
"tests/test_gate_pipeline_topology_cli.py -- the git init path in
test_backlog_only_workspace_succeeds" as one of the two check=True git
subprocess sites. That file contains NO subprocess.run/check=True call at
all (verified: zero matches for both patterns anywhere in the file); its
victim-#1 failure (test_backlog_only_workspace_succeeds) is an ASSERTION
FAILURE (code 1 != 0), not a bare CalledProcessError, and 149-S already
correctly handled it as a containment/anchoring fix. Per 141.001-T's own
recorded, verbatim, evidence-based diagnostic capture (which this task's
"do not edit without evidence from the recorded reproducing pair" mandate
requires deferring to over a task description's prose), the ACTUAL two
check=True git subprocess sites producing bare CalledProcessError ERRORS
are:
1. tests/test_repo_root_artifacts.py::RepoRootTrackedJsonAllowlistTest::test_root_tracked_json_matches_allowlist
   (`subprocess.run([git, "ls-files", ...], capture_output=True, check=True)`)
2. tests/test_telemetry_gitignore_template.py::MetricsEmissionHardGateTests._git
   (the shared helper, `subprocess.run(["git", *args], ..., check=True)`)
-- exactly matching the two `ERROR:` (not `FAIL:`) entries in every full-suite
run this shipment chain has captured. Fixed these two ACTUAL sites.

## Changes (both N5 -- subprocess arguments and failure-message construction)

1. tests/test_repo_root_artifacts.py: wrapped the `git ls-files` call in
   try/except CalledProcessError; on failure, calls `self.fail(...)` with a
   message embedding the captured (bytes-decoded) stderr verbatim.
2. tests/test_telemetry_gitignore_template.py: wrapped the shared `_git`
   helper's subprocess.run in the same try/except pattern; on failure,
   `self.fail(...)` embeds the captured stderr verbatim. Covers every git
   invocation this test class makes through the helper (init, config x2,
   add, commit).

## Verification (Step 3 -- deliberately forced, not committed)

Removed `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2` from the shell environment (the exact
mechanism 141.001-T identified as the root external cause) and re-ran each
fixed test in isolation:

- test_repo_root_artifacts.py: `AssertionError: git ls-files failed (exit
  128) while checking the root-level tracked JSON allowlist; captured
  stderr: 'error: missing config value GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2\nfatal: unable to
  parse command-line config\n'`
- test_telemetry_gitignore_template.py: `AssertionError: git init failed
  (exit 128); captured stderr: 'error: missing config value
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2\nfatal: unable to parse command-line config\n'`

Both messages surface the exact verbatim stderr 141.001-T originally
captured via its ad-hoc diagnostic wrapper -- confirming the fix works as
intended. This forced-failure state was NOT committed; both files were
restored to their normal (env-intact) passing state before commit.

## AIG (assertion-integrity gate)

AIG-1: zero `self.assert*`/`assertRaises`/`pytest.raises` lines touched in
either file (verified via `git diff main` -- the only new `self.` call is
`self.fail(...)`, which is not part of the assertion-callsite set AIG-1
defines). AIG-3/AIG-4: every changed line in both files is class N5.

## Isolation pass-count parity (AC-c)

Both modules, before (git stash to original) vs after (this fix): Ran 7
tests ... OK in BOTH cases, identical pass count, no assertion weakened.

AC-a: satisfied (both check=True sites now surface captured stderr
verbatim in the failure message, verified by deliberate forced failure).
AC-b: satisfied (AIG above).
AC-c: satisfied (isolation parity above).
AC-d: hosted CI will be confirmed on the PR.
